You are implementing ticket 14 of the Email OS maintenance programme: run fixture mode on the Gmail core with a built-in synthetic provider, so the operation ledger (acceptance, undo, groups, reminders) exists once in Rust instead of twice. You do stages 1 to 3 of ADR 0002 in this thread. Stage 4 (switching the default and deleting the old backend) is NOT yours: you stop after stage 3 and report.

I am the coordinating thread. I gate and merge your PRs; you never merge. You can message me at any time with a question, and you should message me when each stage's PR is ready so I can gate it while you continue.

## Read first

- `docs/adr/0002-fixture-as-synthetic-provider.md` — the whole thing. Its behaviour inventory table and its appendix (the test disposition, test by test) are your specification.
- `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/development.md`, `docs/current-status.md`, `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` if present.
- `crates/mail-core/src/gmail/` — `sync.rs` (GmailCore, `open_with_clock`, the worker), `types.rs` (trait `GmailProvider`; the live implementation is `LiveGmailProvider` in `provider.rs`), `store.rs` and `store/` (18 modules), `store_schema.rs` (ordered migrations, currently `gmail-migrations-9`).
- The fixture side you are replacing later: `crates/mail-core/src/lib.rs` (`MailCore`), `store.rs`, `worker.rs`, `seed.rs`, `provider.rs`, `store/reminders.rs`; and `src-tauri/src/main.rs` (`Backend` enum).
- `crates/mail-core/src/testing.rs` and `testing/` (the `test-support` feature: temp profiles, bounded waits, scripted provider).
- The contract scenarios merged today: `tests/fixtures/contract-scenarios/`, `crates/mail-core/tests/contract_scenarios.rs` (profiles `gmail` and `fixture`, `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES`), `tests/browser-fake/contract-scenarios.test.ts`, `tests/support/contract-scenarios.ts`, and the doc that describes the format.
- The prototype branch `origin/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype` is evidence only. Do not merge or copy it wholesale; the ADR lists what it got wrong (non-atomic JSON facts, per-conversation archive, readiness shims).

## Decisions already made

The ADR is merged with Status "Proposed". The project owner asked for the remaining tickets to run, and I am proceeding on these decisions. In your first PR, record them in the ADR under a short "Decisions" section and change the status to "Accepted (stages 1–3)". Word it accurately: these were taken on the coordinator's recommendation, and the owner can still redirect before stage 4.

1. Go with staged unification, as the ADR recommends.
2. Synthetic fixture mode admits archive, read and star (single and group), and the cached Starred list works. This departs from the ADR's "archive-only" wording, which was about preserving today's errors; the decision is that the unified fixture gains read and star. Cached Trash and provider destinations stay rejected with today's error variants. Connect, disconnect, permission upgrade and manual sync stay rejected with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`, and nothing in synthetic mode may erase local state the way a Gmail disconnect does.
3. Synthetic reminders follow the Gmail core's local rules (hide locally, no provider write). The fixture's archive/restore reminder phases are retired when stage 4 lands, not before.
4. The on-disk transition (stage 4) will be a one-time reset with disclosure and a retained backup, local drafts untouched. You do not implement it; you plan it.

Everything else in the ADR's table stands: wire mode stays `fixture`, the account stays `fixture-account`, no OAuth, no Keychain, no HTTP client, cached-only search, all 18 conversations present including the two initially archived ones (`conv-06`, `conv-15`), the fake pause/reject environment controls apply only to synthetic writes and never reach the live provider.

## Hard rules

- **Default behaviour does not change in stages 1 to 3.** With no opt-in set, fixture mode still runs `MailCore` on `fixture-profile/mail.db`, byte for byte as today. Existing fixture tests stay and stay green. Nothing is deleted from the old backend in this thread.
- **Gmail behaviour does not change at all.** The session policy must be a no-op for Gmail. Existing Gmail tests are not edited to make them pass (adding tests is fine; a mechanical signature change is fine if you list every one). Prefer no change to the Gmail database schema. If you truly need one, it is an ordered migration step 10 with a legacy fixture and updated `current-schema.sql`, following `store_schema.rs` and `migration_tests.rs`, and you tell me before you build on it.
- The synthetic provider is production code. It must not enable or import the `test-support` feature. The dependency direction is testing → production. Move the 18-conversation data into a production synthetic module in a way that the old `seed.rs` path keeps working unchanged (share the data, do not fork it).
- Synthetic provider facts must be durable and crash-safe (transactional, not a JSON file rewritten in place), must model archive per message as Gmail does, and must be seeded once: reopening must never overwrite facts that changed. Its storage lives under the fixture profile, in a new file. It never touches `mail.db`, the `gmail-profile`, credentials, or `local-drafts`.
- No DTO shape, generated TypeScript, IPC command name or event name changes. Run `mise run check:contract`.
- Privacy: nothing that logs may include subjects, addresses, bodies, tokens, URLs with ids, or SQL with bound values. Storage errors go through `storage_log.rs` as they do today.
- Synthetic data only. No real accounts, credentials or Google network, in code or tests. Tests use injected clocks and event barriers, not wall-clock sleeps.
- Do not touch these frontend files; another PR (#34) that changes them merges within the hour: `src/App.vue`, `src/components/`, `src/assets/style.css`, `src/lib/account-status.ts`, `src/lib/action-palette.ts`, `src/lib/browsing-actions.ts`, `src/FixtureWorkspaces.vue`, `tests/account*`, `tests/layout/`. The only frontend files you should need are `src/lib/ipc/browser-fake.ts` and the contract scenario tests. If you believe you need another, ask me first.
- Do not change the Gmail worker's behaviour after a definite failure (known divergence KD-1 in `contract_scenarios.rs`). That is waiting on the owner.

## The three stages, one PR each

Stack the branches (`maintenance/p4-synthetic-stage1`, `-stage2`, `-stage3`). The stage 1 PR targets `main`; the others target the branch below. CI only runs on PRs whose base is `main`, so each stage must pass `mise run check:all` locally before you mark its PR ready. Open each PR as a draft and mark it ready when green. Message me when each one is ready.

**Stage 1 — port the guarantees, add the provider.**
- Record the decisions in the ADR (above).
- Production synthetic data module and `SyntheticGmailProvider` implementing `GmailProvider`, constructed directly, with durable facts.
- Port the fixture guarantees to tests that run against `GmailCore` + the synthetic provider, following the ADR appendix test by test. Keep a table in the PR description: each appendix entry → the new test, or "obsolete under decision N", or "deferred to stage 2/3 because …". Nothing silently dropped.
- Fix known divergence KD-3 on the fake's side: undo on a group whose members are all ineligible is accepted by both Rust stores with members marked skipped, and rejected by the browser fake with `not_applicable`. Align the fake to Rust, remove the `KNOWN_DIVERGENCES` entry (the runner tells you if an entry no longer fails), and keep that in its own commit.

**Stage 2 — explicit session policy and seeding.**
- An explicit internal session policy in `GmailCore` (not a scattering of `if fixture` checks): identity and status (`fixture` mode, `fixture-account`, connected/idle presentation per the ADR table, no mutation "grant" masquerading as a Google permission), admission (decision 2), lifecycle rejections, cached-only search, local readiness in place of the `has_credentials()` restore signal, and non-destructive lifecycle. Gmail's policy is the existing behaviour, unchanged.
- Seed-once bootstrap that finishes before the session reports ready, including the two initially archived conversations, without pretending they are Inbox mail. Initially archived rows are not Done evidence.
- No needless periodic synthetic discovery, or make a stable empty history cheap. Fake pause/reject must not stall reads or bootstrap.
- Add a `synthetic` profile to the Rust contract scenario runner and run every scenario on it. It should match the `gmail` profile except where the policy says otherwise; any difference is either a named, justified entry or a bug you fix. KD-2 (fixture `setRead` errors) concerns the old `fixture` profile and stays listed until stage 4; note in the PR what the fake will need at stage 4.

**Stage 3 — reminders, attachments, reply metadata, opt-in launch.**
- Reminders on the synthetic session under the Gmail local rules, with acceptance, race and restart tests (injected clock). Fresh reads come from the durable synthetic provider.
- The synthetic `fixture-text` attachment (same descriptor, filename, exact bytes, limits, exact-target revalidation, cancellation) and deterministic reply metadata (including the hostile literal bodies, sender identity and references) served through the provider/core seams rather than fabricated in the shell. The shell's transfer security stays common. The old shell path keeps working for the default backend.
- An opt-in launch path: an environment variable (suggest `EMAIL_OS_SYNTHETIC_CORE=1`, fixture mode only, ignored in Gmail mode) that makes the shell run fixture mode on `GmailCore` + the synthetic provider with its own database file under the fixture profile. `local-drafts` is shared and untouched, `mail.db` is never opened for writing on this path. Document it in `docs/development.md` as a validation path, not a user feature. I will run my native smoke test on it, so the 18 conversations, archive, undo, reader, search, drafts and reminders must work end to end through the real Tauri commands. Add native bridge tests in `src-tauri` for it.

## Then stop and report

Do not start stage 4. Your final report must include:
- The three PRs with head SHAs, and for each: test counts for `mail-core`, `email-os` and the frontend (baseline on main today: 328, 14, and 1,527 in 89 files), and confirmation `check:all` passed.
- The appendix disposition table, complete.
- Every existing test you edited, with the reason.
- A stage 4 plan: the switch, the disclosure and backup-reset design (cancel, crash/restart, insufficient disk, backup failure), exactly what gets deleted, and what the browser fake and docs need.
- A UI impact inventory for stage 4: every user-visible difference between today's fixture mode and the synthetic one (status values, loading states, read/star controls appearing, reminder phases, error text, anything else you found), each with where in the frontend it surfaces.
- What you could not verify.

## Working on this machine

- 2 cores, 7 GB RAM, about 6 GB of free disk, shared with one other agent thread and my gate runs. Run one cargo build or test at a time, never two in parallel, and no more than two subagents at once. Use `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/exedev/email-os/target` (the shared target directory) for every cargo and mise invocation; do not create another target directory. If free disk drops under 2 GB, stop and message me.
- Do not modify the working tree of the root checkout `/home/exedev/email-os` (it has an uncommitted change that belongs to the owner). Work only in your worktree.
- Run `pnpm install` in your worktree before frontend checks. Tasks are in `mise.toml`: `test:core`, `test:native`, `test:ui`, `check:contract`, `lint:core`, `lint:native`, `typecheck`, `build:web`, `check:all`.
- Use subagents for self-contained pieces (for example, porting one appendix section of tests, or an independent review of the session policy diff before you mark stage 2 ready). Subagents run on the same model as you. Give them the hard rules above.
- After each push, confirm the remote head matches your local head (`git ls-remote`). `gh` commands need `-R BbrSofiane/email-os`.
- If an existing test fails intermittently, do not retry it into silence: tell me which and what you saw.
- If a hard rule and the ADR conflict, or a stage turns out to need something this brief forbids, stop and ask me rather than choosing.
I'll start by reading the ADR and the surrounding docs.

1	# ADR 0002: Fixture mode as a synthetic provider
2	
3	**Status:** Proposed
4	
5	## Question and recommendation
6	
7	Investigate replacing the native fixture store/worker with `GmailCore` and a built-in, credential-free `SyntheticProvider`. This is a decision spike, not authorization to change production behavior. Baseline: `58e0bc7`.
8	
9	**Recommendation: GO for staged unification; NO-GO for an unmodified provider-only substitution.** GmailCore already accepts `Arc<dyn GmailReadProvider>` and an injected clock. The provider must own durable synthetic provider facts; the core needs a small explicit fixture policy for mode/capabilities/lifecycle and reminders. Keeping a second operation ledger is avoidable, but silently changing the fixture contract is not acceptable. After those gates, delete the fixture `Store`, worker, reminder implementation and `MailCore` facade, and hold one `GmailCore` in shell state with a session policy instead of the `Backend` enum. Move the 18-conversation data out of `seed.rs` into the synthetic module before deleting that file. Retain shared `CancelToken` infrastructure currently located in `provider.rs`; removing the old archive fake must not remove Gmail cancellation support.
10	
11	## Evidence checkpoints
12	
13	- Required architecture, status, development and ADR 0001 read. Current docs explicitly promise a separate durable native fixture profile, seed-once behavior, archive-only mailbox actions, local drafts and synthetic attachment transfers.
14	- `gmail/sync.rs::open_with_clock` has no direct OAuth/Keychain dependency: those belong to the injected production `GmailProvider`. Startup currently interprets `has_credentials()` as a restore signal; a synthetic implementation needs an explicit local-ready policy rather than inventing real credentials.
15	- `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` hardcodes `MailMode::Gmail`; `mutation_access()` is a Boolean grant covering archive/read/star. Neither preserves fixture wire behavior by itself.
16	- All requested fixture test files were inventoried by test function name (appendix below). No production files are changed by this spike.
17	
18	## Implementation stages (each must remain green and shippable)
19	
20	1. Port fixture-specific guarantees to tests against GmailCore, retain both existing backends, and add a production synthetic data/provider module independent of test support. Keep the default fixture path unchanged.
21	2. Introduce explicit internal session policy in GmailCore: fixture identity/status, archive-only admission, unsupported errors, cached-only search, local readiness and non-destructive lifecycle. Implement persistent synthetic provider facts and seed-once discovery including the two initially archived conversations. Keep Gmail policy unchanged.
22	3. Resolve reminder behavior explicitly and cover it with acceptance/race/restart tests; move synthetic attachments/reply metadata behind provider/core seams. Preserve local drafts and fixture profile safety. Add opt-in synthetic-core launch path for validation.
23	4. Switch fixture default only after all mapped guarantees pass and profile transition disclosure is implemented. Keep the old database as backup. Remove the legacy backend after parity validation; update current docs and browser contract tests. Coordinating thread owns end-to-end validation and merge sequencing.
24	
25	## Risks and decision gates
26	
27	A fresh provider seeded into memory on every launch can overwrite archived provider facts at the next sync. Gmail discovery only lists Inbox, so it cannot by itself reproduce the two archived seed threads. GmailCore may expose read/star or destructive disconnect if fixture mode is represented as Gmail. Reminder scheduling currently has different mailbox effects. These are design gates for implementation, not bugs established by this spike.
28	
29	The prototype will be published separately at [maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype](https://github.com/BbrSofiane/email-os/tree/maintenance/p4-synthetic-provider-prototype), marked throwaway and not for merge. This PR contains only this ADR.
30	
31	## Behavior inventory and required policy
32	
33	References are repository-relative; function names identify the reviewed seam. **Blocker** means an unmodified provider-only substitution cannot preserve the contract. It does not mean the staged implementation is infeasible.
34	
35	| Surface | Fixture today / GmailCore with synthetic provider | Classification and implementation condition |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Account/status | `src-tauri/src/main.rs::Backend::account_status` returns fixture/Connected/Idle, no mutation grant, 18 cached, complete, no timestamp, limit 0. `gmail/sync.rs::account_status` returns Gmail, observed grant, transient Authenticating/Syncing, timestamps and limit 100. | **Blocker** to drop-in. Internal fixture policy must retain fixture mode/identity/capability presentation; disclose initial loading if asynchronous bootstrap is retained. Do not masquerade as a connected Google account. |
38	| Credentials | Fixture never opens OAuth or Keychain. GmailCore only calls provider methods; shell constructs GmailProvider/Keychain only in Gmail branch. `gmail/types.rs::GmailReadProvider` does not require a secret type. | **Same** possible. Synthetic provider is constructed directly, with no HTTP client or Secrets. Explicit local-ready startup should replace the misleading credential-presence signal in production. |
39	| Lifecycle | Fixture rejects connect/disconnect/upgrade/sync commands with `InvalidRequest { field: "mode" }`. Gmail disconnect cancels work and clears account/cache. | **Blocker** without fixture admission policy. Preserve errors and prevent synthetic disconnect from erasing local state. |
40	| Mailbox gates | Fixture archives/restores, rejects read/star singles/groups with `ReadOnly`; some other unsupported commands use mode errors. GmailCore's Boolean mutation grant admits all three dimensions (`accept_action`, `accept_operation`). | **Blocker**. Per-session archive-only gate is required at core admission, not only hidden controls. Retain existing error variants initially; consistency is a separate contract change. |
41	| Fake controls | `provider.rs::FakeArchiveProvider::from_env`: paused blocks writes cancellation-aware; reject rejects the next write once; success/default succeeds. | **Different-but-acceptable** implementation: preserve exact environment semantics only in SyntheticProvider writes, leaving reads/bootstrap responsive. Never route the variable to GmailProvider. |
42	| Seed/restart | `store.rs::migrate_and_seed` transaction seeds `conv-01`…`conv-18` once, including archived `conv-06`/`conv-15`; restarts retain facts/history. Gmail discovery fetches Inbox and does not seed archived rows. | **Blocker** without durable synthetic provider state and initial all-seed cache import. A one-time synthetic bootstrap must preserve actual Inbox facts. Existing `GmailCore::load_search_conversation` / `GmailStore::save_search` can preload the two archived seeds explicitly without pretending they are Inbox mail. Ordinary discovery/history intentionally excludes uncached archived bodies (`history_does_not_import_new_archived_thread_bodies_into_the_bounded_cache`). Reopening an in-memory default provider is insufficient. |

grep -rn "KD-3\|U16" docs src tests crates --include=* -l 2>/dev/null | head; git add -A src tests && git commit -q -m "fix: browser fake accepts an Undo attempt on an all-ineligible group like the Rust stores

Both Rust stores accept the attempt as the group's one attempt with every
member skipped (typed reasons) while the status advertises undo unavailable.
The fake rejected the attempt with not_applicable. Split the fake's group
blocker into the attempt rules (already_undone, expired, superseded; a
group with no accepted child never holds the action slot) and the
availability rule (adds not_applicable when no member is eligible), remove
the KD-3 entries from the contract scenario divergences, and update the one
fake test that asserted the old rejection.
